A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Brep2Shape study. All main-text and appendix material is readable, allowing reliable matching of text, equations, tables, and figures despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original pre-training scaling experiments, downstream classification and segmentation results, ablations, and repeated-seed evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds quantitative representation comparisons, a Q-Former comparison, and downstream pre-training ablation results.

M1.justification: The Bezier decomposition, reconstruction objective, tokenizers, Dual Transformer, topology attention, and downstream adaptation procedure remain unchanged. Q-Former is an added experimental comparator, not a revised proposed model.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Brep2Shape-250k sources and downstream datasets, including the MFCAD domain-transfer evaluation. The added diagnostics use existing datasets and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 adds a Q-Former with query-based cross-attention to the backbone comparison in v1 Table 4. The existing backbone comparators, main benchmark baselines, and SSL4CAD domain-transfer comparator are retained.

E3.justification: v2 introduces quantitative representation-evaluation protocols: randomly selecting 20 faces, comparing label agreement among the top and bottom 10% by cosine similarity, and training a single-layer MLP on each frozen representation. Existing training budgets, model configurations, and evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: Existing model analysis is extended with quantitative representation diagnostics in Table 8, a Q-Former fusion ablation, and downstream outcomes for pre-training ablations in Appendix B.3. The fine-tuning strategy and epoch-sweep analyses already existed in v1's appendix and are relocated.

E5.justification: v1 Table 12 and v2 Table 14 report the same three seeds, means, and standard deviations. Changing 'Standard derivation' to 'Standard Deviation' corrects terminology without changing statistical practice. The new diagnostics do not add uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New results include Q-Former's 0.8244 TMCAD accuracy, representation discriminability scores of 0.14/0.21/0.23 and probe accuracies of 0.7035/0.7353/0.8465 for boundary/shape/Brep2Shape representations, and downstream pre-training ablation scores. Matched main benchmark results remain unchanged; the relocated epoch sweep merely converts proportions to percentages.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 newly defines a discriminability score as the difference in label-agreement rates between the most and least similar 10% of faces. This limited metric definition accompanies the new evaluation; the geometric definitions, decomposition derivations, and Theorem D.1 with its proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about representation alignment, the Dual Transformer, scalability, accuracy, and convergence. The additional experiments support existing contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 expands explanations of why feature fusion affects classification and segmentation differently. Its discussion of the retained epoch sweep shifts from diminishing returns to continued adaptation, preserved geometric knowledge, and no clear overfitting. Case-study interpretations are expanded, while Appendix F's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code repository link in the abstract and removes Appendix A.1's promise to release the pre-training dataset upon acceptance. The PDFs do not establish the dataset's release status. Existing implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and runtime disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works, and the stated positioning relative to continuous, discrete, and self-supervised B-rep methods remain unchanged. The Q-Former ablation adds no citation or revised novelty claim.

P1.justification: Section 4.3 receives localized rewriting and expanded explanations, incorporating the former appendix fine-tuning strategy and dynamics analyses. v2 also updates publication front matter, adds disclosures and acknowledgements, and corrects typos; the broader narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 8 and 13, extends the backbone table, and reformats the two fine-tuning tables moved into the main text. Existing figures retain their content, while appendix Figures 9 and 10 are redistributed across pages. These are limited display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens specific evidentiary links: Table 8 supplements qualitative representation visualization with quantitative comparisons, and Table 13 connects pre-training ablations to downstream performance. The Q-Former control and code-access link also help. These are incremental gains; new analyses lack uncertainty and detailed configuration reporting, stronger mechanistic interpretations remain indirect, and removal of the data-release promise leaves dataset access unresolved.
